_about: Wording a person has approved. 'pins' puts votes at the top of the home page for 90 days. 'votes' sets the name, outcome and one-line explanation for a vote, and always wins over AI or automatic wording. 'carried' marks a bill the Senate is using to carry a different, larger package: Senate vote pages on or after 'since' show the note in place of the summary of the original bill, and the bill page shows the note at the top. 'bills' holds a one-sentence and a short summary a person wrote from the bill's text; it replaces the AI summary. 'reviewed' lists bills whose text changed a lot and whose summary a person has checked against the latest text, with the date and what was checked.

2026-317.name: Hegseth impeachment
2026-317.plain: The House voted to send the impeachment of the Defense Secretary to a committee instead of voting on it. One Republican sided with Democrats to keep it alive.

2026-320.name: Veterans' disability pay
2026-320.plain: The House pulled a bill out of committee that would let veterans with combat-related disabilities collect both disability and retirement pay.

2026-307.name: Iran war powers
2026-307.plain: The House directed the President to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran.

s2026-257.name: Energy permitting bill: first vote to take it up
s2026-257.plain: The Senate voted 73 to 25 to move toward debate on H.R. 2347, a House tax bill that Senate leaders are using to carry a large energy permitting package. The package would change permit and environmental review rules for energy projects and power lines.

s2026-258.name: Energy permitting bill: vote to begin debate
s2026-258.plain: The Senate voted 62 to 21 to begin debate on H.R. 2347, a House tax bill that Senate leaders are using to carry a large energy permitting package. The package was then offered as an amendment that would replace the bill's text.

s2026-264.name: Energy permitting bill: vote to end debate on the package
s2026-264.plain: The Senate voted 70 to 27 to end debate on a large energy permitting package, offered as a replacement for the text of H.R. 2347, a House tax bill. The 60 votes needed were reached.

s2026-266.name: Energy permitting bill: setting aside budget rules
s2026-266.plain: The Senate voted 70 to 26 to set aside budget rules for H.R. 2347, a House tax bill carrying a large energy permitting package, so it could move forward. The 60 votes needed were reached.

s2026-267.name: Energy permitting bill: adding the package
s2026-267.plain: The Senate voted 69 to 27 to replace the text of H.R. 2347, a House tax bill, with a large energy permitting package called the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. The package changes permit and environmental review rules for energy projects and power lines. It keeps the original tax bill as its last part.

s2026-268.name: Energy permitting bill: vote to end debate
s2026-268.plain: The Senate voted 65 to 31 to end debate on H.R. 2347, a House tax bill, after its text was replaced with a large energy permitting package. The 60 votes needed were reached.

s2026-270.name: Energy permitting bill
s2026-270.plain: The Senate voted 62 to 33 to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, a large energy permitting package carried in H.R. 2347, a House tax bill. It sets deadlines for federal permits and environmental reviews, limits the time to file many lawsuits against them, and changes rules for power lines and other energy projects. It also keeps the original tax bill, which would stop taxing most payouts won by survivors of sexual abuse. The bill now goes to the House.

2026-325.name: Thomas Paine memorial near the National Mall
2026-325.plain: The House passed a bill, 365 to 36, approving a location for the memorial to Thomas Paine, author of Common Sense. It would go in the central area of Washington around the National Mall that is reserved for works of lasting national significance.

s2026-269.name: Directing the President to end hostilities against Iran
s2026-269.plain: The Senate voted 48 to 51 against a resolution directing the President to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or specifically authorizes the use of force. Forces needed to defend the U.S., an ally, or a partner from imminent attack would not be covered. The House passed the resolution on September 15, 2026.

s2026-272.name: Richard Wesley Bennett for U.S. District Judge for the Southern District of Texas

hr-2347.note: The Senate used this House tax bill to carry a much larger energy permitting package, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. Senate votes on H.R. 2347 since November 9, 2026 are votes on that package. On November 18, 2026, the Senate replaced the bill's text with the package, and on November 19 it passed the bill, 62 to 33. The package changes permit and environmental review rules for energy projects and power lines, and keeps the original tax bill as its last part. The summary of the original House bill does not describe it.

s-1383.note: The Senate passed this bill as the Veterans Accessibility Advisory Committee Act. On February 11, 2026 the House replaced all of its text with the SAVE America Act, which would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote and photo identification to vote in federal elections. Senate votes on S. 1383 after that date are about the House version.

s-1318.note: The Senate passed this bill as the Fallen Servicemembers Religious Heritage Restoration Act. On April 29, 2026 the House replaced all of its text with a bill on foreign surveillance and a ban on a Federal Reserve digital currency. Senate votes on S. 1318 after that date are about the House version.

s-1318.one_sentence: As changed by the House, this bill would extend a foreign surveillance law to April 30, 2029, add checks on FBI searches for Americans' information, and bar the Federal Reserve from issuing its own digital currency.
s-1318.short: The Senate passed this bill as the Fallen Servicemembers Religious Heritage Restoration Act, about grave markers for American-Jewish servicemembers buried overseas. On April 29, 2026 the House replaced all of its text. The new text extends Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, which includes Section 702, from April 30, 2026 to April 30, 2029. It requires a monthly civil liberties review of FBI searches for Americans' information, requires an attorney to approve those searches, and sets up to 5 years in prison for FBI employees who knowingly and willfully break the search rules. It also bars the Federal Reserve from issuing, testing or developing a central bank digital currency.
